note: Files: s3 r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (cached at runs/theory-tests/duel-r4-m08/base01_F_hard.jsonl) and r3/s2800-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (cached as s2800_P_hard.jsonl); overlap file is studies/rlneurons/results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the recipe's results/rln3/... path is relative to the rlneurons study; no file exists at the repo-root path). Overlap flags under sets.hard.flags are keyed by problem_index, not unique_id, so the 328 filter and the post/pre source label are looked up through each row's problem_index (checked while reading the format: every row's unique_id prefix matches the overlap source). Both files have exactly one row per unique_id (sample 0), so the smallest-sample rule changes nothing. right = score == 1, and a null score counts as 0. Strata are cut on the RL row's n_generated, ties broken by unique_id, 4 groups of floor(n/4) with the remainder in the last group. A stratum with pre problems but no post problems gets w=0, so it adds nothing to either G. A stratum with post problems but no pre problems is dropped and w is renormalised. Only 60 post problems (AIME 2025 + HMMT Feb 2025), so each stratum holds few post items and the number is noisy. alt_measured is a different statistic, not another reading: the unstratified gap 100*(mean d_post - mean d_pre) with no length matching. The recipe left no real ambiguity to read two ways.

Same files, 328 filter (via problem_index), join and post/pre labels as k=1. Kept: score == 1 in both rows and cap_hit is False in both. r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median(pre r) - median(post r), even counts averaged. If no post problem survives, the script recomputes without the cap_hit condition (stderr reports whether that happened). If a group is still empty the script prints not_computable, because the recipe does not say what to do then. alt_measured uses n_new instead of n_generated (n_generated = n_new + 1 in the rows seen), so it should differ only slightly. The post group is small (at most 60 problems, fewer both-right), so the post median is noisy.

Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json per_row.T2 and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, both committed. e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Rows with n_own missing or 0, or sum_entropy_own missing, are dropped. Join on problem_index. Kept: t2_right true (stored as int 1, so 1 is treated as true) and t2_cap_hit False. Split on per_problem t2_generated_tokens (<= 2000 short, > 2000 long). Ratio = median short / median long. alt_measured normalises by n_gen instead of n_own (n_own = n_gen + 1 in the rows seen), so it is only a tiny variant. Note: these are T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 generations, and the entropies come from teacher-forcing the stored answers under the RL model (own), as the checks.json fields name them.
